messages:
ida (customer): hey support, bit urgent — after accepting the org invite from our Okta flow i can see the organization but getting a 403 when i try to open the project details page. says "You don't have permission to view this project". i accepted via the magic link yesterday.

samira (support): hi ida :wave: can you confirm which project id you're trying to access and whether you used the same email as your org invite? also, do you see the project in the left nav at all or is it missing entirely?

ida (customer): project id 6732. it shows up in the org list but clicking it -> 403. i accepted with ida+sales@example.com (we use plus addressing). we do SCIM group->role mapping.

samira (support): thanks. two quick checks: 1) can you paste the exact error text from the devtools network response (no tokens). 2) can you confirm whether you can see your role under org settings -> members?

ida (customer): network response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "You do not have permission to view project 6732"
}
```
i do not see any role next to my name under members — it just shows my email and "pending" previously, but after accept it shows no role.

samira (support): weird. i can see a recent SCIM sync for your org (org-882). could be two things: 1) idp claim used for mapping got altered/truncated during SSO assertion, or 2) SCIM group->role mapping didn't include the plus-addressed email. can you confirm if your user is part of the SCIM group that should map to "project-developer"?

ida (customer): yes, i am in the Okta group(s) that should map. our admin says the group list in Okta was very long.

jordan (sre): jumping in — tagging eng here. i suspect the IdP is truncating the SAML/JWT group attribute when it exceeds a size threshold, which would mean Redwood never receives the expected group membership and mapping fails, resulting in no role assignment -> 403. seen this with large orgs.

li (idp-infra): lab note: okta has a known behavior where the `groups` SAML attribute can be truncated if the raw payload exceeds an internal length. also plus-address normalization in some orgs can rewrite the NameID/email. can you dump the decoded token or SAML assertion? please redact PII.

ida (customer): how do i dump that? our IT can get the assertion logs.

samira (support): if you can get the SAML assertion or the decoded JWT from your IdP, please paste the attribute block for `groups` / `roles` (redact group ids). example we need to see if the role string is complete or ends with `...` or truncated. also, if Okta rewrote the email, we might be matching on a different identifier.

ida (customer): IT pasted the assertion — groups attribute ends in `...` (literally truncated) and my email is `ida@example.com` in one place and `ida+sales@example.com` in NameID.

jordan (sre): ok that explains it. SCIM had created membership for ida+sales@example.com but our SSO pipeline was matching on the NameID (ida@example.com) after canonicalization — mismatch so we were never mapping to the SCIM membership. and the truncated groups attribute meant the mapping by group name failed too.

samira (support): immediate workaround: org admin can manually assign "project-developer" to your account from org -> members -> find user -> edit roles. that should unblock you while we sort the IdP mapping. did admin confirm they can do that?

ida (customer): admin applied manual role and i can access the project now, thanks!

li (idp-infra): long-term fix options: 1) update Okta to send a dedicated `roles` attribute rather than relying on the concatenated `groups` claim, or 2) switch SCIM to authoritative group sync (we already support SCIM group sync mapping rather than `groups` claim); either avoids the length/truncation issue. also ensure the SAML NameID/email attribute used by Redwood is the immutable IdP user id (not the display email) — prevents plus-address mismatches.

samira (support): openning internal ticket: <https://app.redwood.example/ticket/T-12345|T-12345> — added logs and assertion snippet (redacted). tagging eng-bot for assignment.

eng-bot: assigned to li (idp-infra) — ETA 3d for config guidance and doc update. :pushpin:

jordan (sre): note for playbook — add step to verify IdP `groups` attribute length and NameID canonicalization during onboarding. i'll PR the devex docs.

ida (customer): thanks all — appreciate the quick help and the manual role fix. please let us know when the SCIM recommendation doc is ready.

samira (support): closing loop: root cause = IdP truncated `groups` claim + NameID/email canonicalization mismatch. resolved by manual admin role grant and recommended fixes to IdP config (send explicit `roles` attribute or enable SCIM group sync) — will follow up in T-12345 with exact Okta settings. :lock:
